name: Citizenship by Declaration -- Descendants of Nazi Persecution Victims (§58c StbG)

qualifying_event.description: A 2020 amendment (§58c Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz, in force since 1 September 2020) lets direct-line descendants of a person who left Austria before 15 May 1955 due to well-founded fear of, or actual, Nazi-era persecution (or persecution for supporting the Austrian democratic republic) acquire Austrian citizenship by written declaration, without a residence requirement and without renouncing their existing citizenship.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Documentary proof of descent from the persecuted ancestor and of that ancestor's persecution/flight before 15 May 1955; written application to the competent authority (Austria's National Fund may be consulted as an expert body).

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must be a direct-line (any generation) descendant of a person who left Austria before 15 May 1955 due to well-founded fear of, or actual, persecution by Nazi organs/the Third Reich, or for supporting the Austrian democratic republic.
Ancestry and persecution/flight must be shown by unobjectionable documents or other certifying means.

evidence_required.document: Proof of direct-line descent from the persecuted ancestor
Documentary proof of the ancestor's persecution or flight before 15 May 1955

sources.title: Law & Experts (Austrian immigration law firm) -- §58c StbG: direct-line descendants of Nazi persecution victims who fled before 15 May 1955, no residence requirement, dual citizenship explicitly permitted, in force since 1 September 2020
